question: A previously healthy 20-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 15 minutes after collapsing while playing basketball. He has no history of serious illness. On arrival, there is no palpable pulse or respiratory effort observed. He is declared dead. The family agrees to an autopsy. Cardiac workup prior to this patient's death would most likely have shown which of the following findings?

options.opa: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve
options.opb: Narrowing of the left main coronary artery
options.ope: Symmetric thickening of the left ventricle

analysis: Given the sudden collapse and death of a previously healthy young man, the most likely finding on cardiac workup would be symmetric thickening of the left ventricle, indicative of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, a common cause of sudden cardiac death in young individuals.
